I guess it comes down to how serious a show tries to be. A long-running adventure series is just a jolly ride of a rollercoaster, so it should not be taken too seriously. I haven't watched a popular dark fantasy series, but from the short clips I've seen, it seems that it takes itself much more seriously, meaning it has to be right in order to do that properly.

An example would be a show that tries to take itself very seriously. It fails to do so when it shows characters jumping high into the air to make an extra powerful attack, and instead of sidestepping the slash, the opponent tries to block it. Makes no sense at all and is highly inconsistent with its world.

In many shows and movies, you have to ignore some real-world physics in order to enjoy the show. For instance, giant monster films or mecha battles feature extremely large characters who wouldn't be able to stand if the show respected the square-cubic law.

Dark matter can't be seen, which means that if a fictional pirate had a fruit that turned him into dark matter, we wouldn't be able to see it. Rather than being black, he would be invisible. This means that the powers of another character's fruit are closer to being a Logia with dark matter than the pirate's fruit.

Dark matter is NOT an elemental force, but rather a type of matter. So yes, it is stuff, but we don't know what type of stuff it is.

Your link is about gravitational singularities, which is again something hypothetical. We actually don't even know what black holes are, if there is an event horizon or not (which is something recent papers are beginning to question, even the leading figure in black hole research). We think there is a singularity, which is an infinitely small point in the universe with mass. Your link says a singularity is not a state of matter, as in it's not a state normal matter can take. Iron can't become a singularity, but it can be solid and liquid. It's a weird question, to be honest, because matter has to react in some way if it is compressed into infinity, but this just goes to show how strange singularities are.

It does fit the criteria for a Logia, since it's an element in a sense. The problem is that it's hypothetical, meaning we don't know if it even exists at all. We also have no idea what it is or how it behaves. We have only predicted it because we know that a lot of mass is missing in the universe.

I hope you learned something. I suggest you watch this video if you find dark matter interesting. I sure do :D

As for your final question, I have no idea. I've wondered myself, and I guess we won't know unless the creator tells us. The creator would probably just explain it as the main character: "It's a mystery element!"

A final note: Dark matter has nothing to do with black holes. They are completely separate theories that have nothing to do with each other. I guess you could say that it's possible that black holes are formed from dark matter, since the gravitational pull on light would be the same resulting in a black hole. This is highly unlikely though and would not make much sense.

I have a couple of things to say. First off, the character in question is far stronger than you give him credit for, while another character is not nearly as strong as you suggest. The two other characters mentioned are both much stronger than the latter. The only reason this character is threatening and useful for the governing body is due to his special ability. He possesses a type of power that makes him untouchable without a specific counter ability. This means he is stronger than any character lacking that counter and can be used by the governing body against almost any pirate in the first half of the ocean where almost no one has that counter ability.

The other character, on the other hand, was as strong as the main protagonist at the point of their confrontation. I believe he would have defeated the protagonist had he not been so overconfident. The protagonist barely overcame him using advanced techniques, which are not even necessary to defeat the other character once you discover his weakness (liquids), which allows you to hit him. Had the first character used water in a hypothetical fight against the second, he would have won.

A second issue is your list of villains/antagonists. Why do you include certain powerful figures there, when they haven't shown to be "friends" of the main group, or at least helped them at certain points? One of them is the protagonist's idol and thus a great friend, while another is shown to be a friend and rival of that idol (some theories even suggest he is a member of his crew). Another character assisted a key ally at certain points and is also featured in a film as someone who helps the main group. Sure, it's not canon, but it was written by the original creator, which means the characters remain true to their personalities. One character essentially sacrificed himself to save a key ally, which means he is never intended as an antagonist.

Also, if one character is included in your list, why is he not the last one? He is stated several times to be the strongest man alive, so I don't see how other characters would be able to defeat him. And if the other character is the strongest of a certain group, or at least equal in strength to the two mentioned, why is he not ranked accordingly in your list?

To answer your question, no, the first character would not fit better in the earlier part of the ocean. He is too strong and his character is intertwined in political matters which are not even introduced until just before his defeat. A fight between the protagonist and him in that earlier region would not make any sense for either of them.

> which he declined which would never have happened if the character knew he was weaker than the other

Why? Why would the character need to accept joining the other’s crew if he is weaker? I don't see the logic here.

> The protagonist defeated him with luck and that only.

While I agree that the character was stronger than the protagonist at the time, the fight at the end clearly showed that the protagonist had the best fighting skills. Otherwise, he would've been defeated by the character, luck or not. A minor fighter won't suddenly win a fight against a top-tier fighter if he is lucky enough.

> The antagonist nearly killed another character, but only made a tie with the first character?

There is no evidence that the antagonist actually wanted to hurt the first character, let alone kill him. And why would he? On the other hand, his motive for killing or at least hurting the other character is by order of a powerful organization. They didn't know that the first character would be present at the conflict, which means they never gave out the order.

> The first character is so strong that he does not need a specific ability even if he has it.

This is just wrong. That ability is basically "the new essential" in the series. Everybody needs it to fight at a high level, which is evidenced in the protagonist's training. Why does the mentor put so much emphasis on teaching the protagonist that ability, and only that? Because it's the only thing he needs to "level up."

> As for another character, he can transform into a large animal and can use a specific technique... scary, he would be killed in a heartbeat if he was fighting with the first character.

Why? Transforming into a large animal makes him much faster and stronger. The protagonist was able to defeat the first character without any of his advanced techniques, while he was destroyed by another character until he began using them. And then he **still** had a hard time beating him. Even harder than beating the first character. Yes, I agree that the protagonist vs the first character match was quite ridiculous considering that the protagonist had been impaled and dried up beforehand, but nonetheless it proved that the protagonist's fighting skills were superior to the first character's, even without advanced techniques.

> The top-tier fighter is still an antagonist or will be in the future

Why? Because he will need to fight another character? Who says they can't have a friendly rivalry match like that of two other characters?

> A specific character is outright villain

No he is not. He cared for another character, which is evidenced when he speaks to her about a past event. He also helps the main group in a non-canon story, which is written by the creator. Why would the creator make him a friend of the main group if he is a villain? That makes no sense at all.

> The legendary character is not the last one because another character could still defeat him

After he had been impaled by a huge weapon, with his mind elsewhere and with countless other smaller injuries and other opponents. Yeah, a really fair fight. The legendary character is **stated** to be the strongest in the world. How is that consistent with several characters being stronger than him?

> A specific character is as strong as another because of a battle which proves that they are tied in strength.

Agreed, although the second character won it after a long fight giving him a slight edge.

> Another character could deflect an attack and survived the clash between them

Deflecting an attack does **not** make you stronger than your opponent. It shows that it's at least not a clash between an important and strong character vs random fodder, but nothing more than that.

> survived the clash between him and the legendary character before the conflict

The legendary character and the other are not enemies. The very reason that the other joined at the end of the conflict was to help the legendary character. The very reason he did not show up until it was too late was to hold back another powerful character from fighting the legendary character while he was occupied with the main group.

> he could battle with a top-tier fighter and make ties with him with a regular weapon even after he lost a limb

Which the top-tier fighter stated had become boring. Now I wonder why that would be...

> by far the strongest we have seen in the series.

How do you even come to this conclusion? Sure, he may have some impressive abilities, but it is evidenced by the fact that the top-tier fighter does not enjoy fighting him anymore than his weapon skills are not that great after he lost his limb. That would leave him with a great mind but a weakened weapon.
